transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-08-31 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lena (NorthBeacon Cloud Architect), Marcus (NorthBeacon Head of Platform), Imran (NorthBeacon Security)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough):
NorthBeacon is evaluating a private deployment for latency and data residency. Main blockers: regional whitelisting, egress controls through corporate firewall, and a requirement for customer-managed keys. They asked for an architecture diagram and pilot sizing. Redwood AE/SE explained options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and recommended Private with dedicated pool behind privatelink or VPC peering depending on transit gateway constraints.

Topics covered:
- VPC peering and transit gateway constraints
- Private endpoints / privatelink alternatives
- IP planning, CIDR overlap concerns
- Region gating and data residency enforcement
- Egress/NAT and firewall policy implications
- KMS/HSM and audit logs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): okay everyone good morning and thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya here is our solutions engineer. How are you folks?
[00:12] Lena: good, thanks. I'm Lena, cloud arch at NorthBeacon. Marcus and Imran are on as well.
[00:16] Marcus: hi all. Quick ask up front, we need to lock region access — legal requires EU-only processing for a subset of data.
[00:25] Priya (SE): got it. We can restrict model serving to specific regions in Redwood Private, and we have controls to keep logs and KV cache inside your VPC, depending on deployment mode.
[00:34] Imran: real quick, do you support customer-managed KMS? We can't have provider-managed keys for the EU data.
[00:40] Jordan: yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM in certain private deployments. I'll confirm exact KMS types but Priya can speak to the integration pattern.
[00:48] Priya: right, for Private we can either integrate with your KMS over the VPC peering or with a dedicated gateway to the HSM. There are some requirements for route tables and endpoint DNS to keep key traffic internal.
[00:58] Lena: okay. On networking — we have a transit-gateway-heavy topology. We prefer privatelink because peering across TGW gets messy for us. Any limits on number of endpoints?
[01:10] Priya: privatelink is a clean approach, fewer route table changes; the limit is mostly AWS account quotas, but Redwood can work with you on endpoint scaling. downside is you need to manage ENIs and that can add NAT/egress considerations.
[01:25] Marcus: what about latency — privatelink vs peering for inference? We care about sub-30ms p99 for small prompts.
[01:33] Priya: in our tests VPC peering can be slightly lower latency since it's direct, but privatelink is within a single AZ unless you replicate endpoints; for p99 sub-30 it depends on AZ topology and the model size. If you pin to local AZ and use dedicated capacity, we can meet that. we'll propose a pilot config.
[01:50] Lena: got it. Another constraint: our corporate egress gates all outbound traffic, only approved CIDRs are allowed. How do we set egress from Redwood instances into our network?
[02:02] Jordan: we typically publish a set of IP ranges you can allow. For Private you can either have our nodes join your VPC or use privatelink. If nodes are in your VPC, egress is controlled by your own NAT/egress. If using privatelink, egress is more constrained and you need to allow our privatelink ENI IPs.
[02:22] Imran: and logging? we must have audit logs for all requests and response hashes retained for 90 days. is that feasible?
[02:30] Priya: yes. Redwood Console in Private mode ships verbose audit logs to your S3 or SIEM, and we can increase retention. There may be a small agent to forward logs or we can push via your log collector.
[02:42] Marcus: any required port openings on the firewall?
[02:45] Priya: only standard TLS 443 for most flows and for KMS we use the KMS port (443 generally). For health checks you might see some ephemeral high ports depending on your NAT. We'll include a port matrix in the diagram.
[02:58] Lena: about CIDRs, we have overlapping 10.0/8 ranges across accounts — peering might conflict. Can you do NAT translation at your side?
[03:07] Jordan: we have options: 1) ask you to provide a dedicated non-overlapping subnet for Redwood nodes, 2) use privatelink which avoids peering conflicts, or 3) configure 1:1 NAT at the edge — that's more involved but possible for Dedicated. We'll flesh pros/cons in the doc.
[03:28] Imran: is there any chance data egress will touch Redwood control plane in the hosted case? we must avoid that.
[03:35] Jordan: for Redwood Private the control plane can be customer-managed or a private control plane; no customer data needs to leave your VPC except for optional telemetry if you allow it. we'll mark that clearly.
[03:46] Priya: small note — some customers confuse continuous batching/KV cache with persistent storage. we keep KV cache in memory in the serving nodes and if you opt-in to hot prefix caching to an external store that's optional.
[03:58] Lena: ok thanks, that helps. Marcus: do you have a recommended pilot footprint for benchmark?
[04:05] Priya: for gen workloads we usually start with 2 GPUs (A100 eq) for 100–200 concurrent small requests; for evaluation you can test with 2x80GB or 4x40 depending on model. We'll propose a pilot that fits your latency targets.
[04:20] Marcus: great. Any SLA differences between Dedicated vs Private?
[04:24] Jordan: Dedicated comes with reserved capacity and stronger throughput SLAs, Private has more control and can be backed by an enterprise SLA depending on the contract. We'll detail SLA language in the follow-up.
[04:36] Imran: one more — are the private endpoints resolvable via our internal DNS? we need internal FQDNs only.
[04:43] Priya: yes, privatelink endpoints map to internal DNS names and we can push Route53 private hosted zones or use your internal DNS forwarders. We'll note steps for split-horizon.
[04:56] Lena: can you run a quick sketch now on the whiteboard?
[05:00] (screen share)
[05:12] Priya: ok drawing a rough flow — customer VPC with TGW, northbeacon subnet, private endpoint to redwood privatelink, redwood service inside our VPC with ENI into your account. if you want peering instead, redwood nodes live in your subnet and we manage the instance pool.
[05:35] Marcus: (overlap) what about multi-region failover? we need EU-primary and US-secondary but no US processing for EU data unless failover is triggered and logged.
[05:45] Jordan: we support region pinning and can set failover routing. we'd require you to whitelist the failover region and consent to cross-border processing at failover time — we can log and require an approval flow.
[05:57] Lena: ok. any regulatory certs we should be aware of? SOC2 plus ISO 27001 is a must for procurement.
[06:04] Jordan: Redwood has SOC2; for Private we can provide the compliance pack and map controls. We'll attach the certs.
[06:12] Imran: are there data residency artifacts we can include in the contract? a clause that logs and payloads for EU-only stay in EU unless explicit manual failover.
[06:20] Jordan: yes we can draft language around region pinning and explicit failover triggers. We'll loop legal.
[06:27] Lena: great. Anything else?
[06:30] Marcus: curious about costs — if we do Private dedicated pool what is unit of billing? per GPU-hour + egress?
[06:37] Jordan: reserved capacity is by GPU-month plus request/throughput tiers; egress patterns depend on network mode — we'll include a sample estimate in the pilot proposal.
[06:45] Priya: one more technical caveat: if you use privatelink and want sub-ms intra-AZ latency, ensure your app sits in the same AZ as the privatelink ENI; otherwise route across AZs adds a hop.
[06:58] Imran: noted. Also please include the expected audit log format so our ingestion team can map fields.
[07:05] Priya: yes we have a sample CloudTrail/S3 format. We'll attach the sample.
[07:12] Jordan: recap next steps: I'll send the network diagram, CIDR suggestions, and contact for legal/compliance certs. Priya will send pilot sizing and a rough cost estimate. NorthBeacon to provide allowed regions and compliance contact.
[07:26] Lena: thanks. We'll try to get region whitelist by early next week.
[07:30] Jordan: perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites and a benchmarking session if you approve the pilot.
[07:36] Marcus: sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:38] (meeting ends)
